events.text: The branch elders meet in the ancestral hall without you the next morning. Through the paper screen you hear them argue over the register, the fields and the name. Nobody asks you in. At the gate, an old cousin waits with your walking stick.

choices.text: Take the stick and go without a word

effects.log: You take the stick and walk out under the crest you painted yourself. You do not look back at it.

choices.text: Go back in and give them one piece of advice

effects.log: You tell them which of the fields floods in spring. The eldest writes it down. It is the last thing the house takes from you.

choices.text: Bow to the tablets one last time

effects.log: You light three sticks of incense before the first tablet, your own name on it. Then you go.

events.text: The Elders' Council sends the new head to you before the year is out: a cousin you remember as a boy who stole plums. He bows too low and asks nothing. The ledger of the house has your line in it now, written by someone else's hand.

choices.text: Tell him the house's oldest debt

effects.log: You tell him who the house still owes, and why. He goes pale, then thanks you.

choices.text: Wish him a long tenure and pour the tea

effects.log: You talk of plums. He laughs for the first time since he took the seal.

choices.text: Say nothing of the house at all

effects.log: You speak of the weather. The seat is his to learn. You have other roads.

events.text: On the last step below the gate a junior you once taught runs after you with a bundle: your old practice robe, washed and folded. "The elders say you may come back," the junior says. "They said to say it twice."

effects.log: You tie the bundle to your pack. It weighs nothing, and you feel it every step.
You put the robe back in the junior's hands. "Wear it better than I did."

choices.text: Ask the junior to say it a third time

effects.log: The junior says it a third time, laughing. You laugh too, and go.

events.text: The last of your captains comes to the tent the night the army breaks up. He has his pay and nowhere to go. "We would have followed you to the capital," he says. "We would have followed you into the river."

choices.text: Tell him that is why you stopped

effects.log: You tell him the river is why. He does not understand, and he will be alive next year to try.
You give him the sword you carried at the head of the column. Songs will be made about it, wrong ones.

choices.text: Send him home with a letter to his mother

effects.log: You write it yourself. He reads it on the road and walks faster.

events.text: {npc} keeps the old roof on four pillars standing beside the new halls, and sweeps it every morning. When you pass by, {he} sets out two cushions and does not ask you to teach. {He} asks what you would have done about the east wind.

mem.note: was told what to do about the east wind

effects.log: You tell {him}. {npc} listens, and then does something else, and it works. You are prouder than you expected.

mem.note: was told to ask the wind

effects.log: {npc} sits on the cushion until dusk. {He} does not thank you, which is right.

mem.note: swept the old roof with the founder

effects.log: You sweep side by side and say nothing of the sect. It is the best morning of the year.
